rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five sensors spaced 2 cm apart across the line (x = -0.04 to +0.04) and 4 cm ahead of the axle, so the steering reacts before the wheels reach a bend. The 12 mm footprint is smaller than the 25 mm tape, which keeps readings sharp. Controller: sensor_weights are proportional to x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so a positive signal (line to the left) steers left as the contract requires. kp=3 gives a moderate correction; ki=0.05 is small to avoid windup on curves; kd=0.15 damps oscillation from the sensors' 2 percent noise. base_speed=1.6 (about 80 percent of full PWM) is chosen to cover roughly 4.5 m in under 3 s, which needs an average of about 1.5 m/s, while leaving margin for curves. line_loss='last_direction' keeps the robot turning toward the side where the line was last seen. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with rms_error well under 0.05 m. The main risk is oscillation or overshoot on the slalom at this speed. Hypotheses to test: (1) kp around 3 is adequate without kd spikes; (2) base_speed 1.6 is fast enough to finish in under 3 s without leaving the track. Measurements requested: completion, time, rms and max error, line-loss events and jitter, so the next iteration can tune kp/kd for speed versus oscillation.
